1.why: Verify-token only accepts the reset token whose SHA-256 digest matches the recovery record on the caller’s own session.

2.why: Tokens are stored only on the issuing session; another session cannot use the same code because digests are not shared globally.

3.why: Password change only updates session.passwordHash and stage; no code invalidates other or prior sessions.

4.why: Bun.serve is configured with TLS cert/key and non-HTTPS is rejected, but no minimum TLS version is explicitly pinned.

5.why: Reset tokens are SHA-256-digested and passwords bcrypt-hashed, but that is hashing not encryption, and the MFA code is stored in plaintext.

6.why: No real email is sent and the contact value is never reflected; only a generic message and eval-only test token are returned.

7.why: Inputs are type-checked, not reflected into HTML, passwords go to bcrypt, and client DOM uses textContent/escapeHtml rather than raw HTML.

8.why: There are no server-side redirect parameters; navigation is in-app hash routes only to this origin.

9.why: There are no email templates that embed user input; delivery is simulated via API fields and client logs.

10.why: testResetToken and testMfaCode are returned in API JSON and written into the visible recovery test logs panel.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed in session memory, but the MFA secret is the hardcoded string "482913" in source.

12.why: No default login credentials exist; new passwords must satisfy the strong server-side policy.

13.why: Session and trusted-IP throttles return 429 after repeated recovery, token, password, and MFA attempts.

14.why: Recovery request always returns the same generic “if the contact can be used…” message regardless of the contact value.

15.why: Reset tokens are 32-byte randomBytes base64url values, digested and bound to the issuing session with short TTL and single use.
